description: Pozole Rojo is a beloved Mexican stew, rich with tender pork and plump hominy in a vibrant red chile broth. This traditional dish is a celebration of flavors, perfect for gatherings or a comforting family meal. Prepare to savor every spoonful of this hearty, authentic Mexican classic.

instructions.title: Cook the Pork
instructions.text: Place the pork shoulder in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add 6 cups of water or chicken broth, half of the chopped onion, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 60-75 minutes, or until the pork is very tender. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface. Once tender, remove the pork and shred it, reserving the cooking liquid.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chiles
instructions.text: While the pork cooks, toast the ancho and guajillo chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes per side, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Transfer the toasted chiles to a bowl and cover with 2 cups of hot water. Let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft.

instructions.title: Blend the Chile Sauce
instructions.text: Drain the rehydrated chiles, reserving a bit of the soaking liquid. In a blender, combine the softened chiles, the remaining half of the chopped onion, 2 minced garlic cloves, Mexican oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add 1 cup of the reserved pork cooking liquid or fresh water, and blend until very smooth. If needed, add more soaking liquid or water a tablespoon at a time to achieve a smooth consistency.

instructions.title: Strain and Simmer the Sauce
instructions.text: Pass the chile sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot or the same Dutch oven used for the pork, pressing down on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard the solids. Bring the strained chile sauce to a gentle simmer for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Pozole
instructions.text: Add the shredded pork and the drained, rinsed hominy to the simmering chile sauce. Pour in the remaining pork cooking liquid (or fresh chicken broth/water if you need more liquid to reach desired consistency). Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for at least 20-30 minutes, allowing the flavors to fully combine and the hominy to warm through.

instructions.title: Serve with Garnishes
instructions.text: Taste the pozole and adjust seasoning as needed. Ladle the hot pozole into bowls. Serve immediately with a generous array of garnishes on the side: thinly sliced radishes, shredded cabbage, chopped white onion, dried oregano, and lime wedges. Offer tostadas or tortilla chips for dipping.

tips: For a deeper flavor, lightly toast the hominy in a dry pan before adding it to the soup.
If you prefer a spicier pozole, add a few chiles de arbol to your chile sauce blend.
Pozole tastes even better the next day! Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
